english.title: Disclose / fail to prevent disclosure of information from a company's PSC register for improper purpose
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being in possession of information obtained by the exercise of a right to inspect or obtain a copy of part or all of the PSC register of **(..SPECIFY COMPANY..) conferred by section 790O of the Companies Act 2006,

(A)_[did something, namely **(..SPECIFY THING DONE..), that resulted in the information being]_
(B)_[failed to do something, namely **(..SPECIFY THING NOT DONE..), with the result that the information was]_

disclosed to another person, namely **(..SPECIFY OTHER PERSON..) knowing, or having reason to suspect, that person may use the information for a purpose that was not a proper purpose
english.legislation: Contrary to section 790R(2) and (3) of the Companies Act 2006.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
being a person in possession of information on a company's PSC register
having inspected or copied it
disclosed that information to another person OR
failed to prevent the disclosure of that information to another person
whom you knew / suspected would use the information for an improper purpose

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: Civil financial penalties may be issued by the registrar for this offence being a ‘relevant offence’ as defined by section 1132A of the Companies Act 2006. No criminal proceedings may be commenced against a person in respect of conduct amounting to an offence if the person has already been given a financial penalty by the registrar. Further, no financial penalty may be imposed on a person in relation to conduct amounting to an offence if proceedings in respect of that offence are ongoing or the person has been convicted.
